subject: Re: Alternate vendor fit scorecard + credit request
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@oakridge.health>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20 09:12 -0700
Subject: Exploring Redwood — can you match a CloudArc offer?

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency profile and quantization options look promising for our agent use cases. We just received a commercial proposal from CloudArc that includes: 40% off list for 12 months + $150k onboarding credit + a six-week dedicated migration engagement. That would be a meaningful head start for our FY27 budget.

Before we take next steps with procurement, can Redwood come back with a comparable package? Specifically: a) any migration/onboarding credits you can offer, b) a committed monthly run-rate discount, and c) an outline of your Dedicated migration support.

I've attached the CloudArc snapshot (PDF) and a short summary of our usage profile. Happy to jump on a quick call if easier. We have a procurement review on 2026-08-26 and would like to finalize terms before then.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Reynolds | VP Product, Oakridge Health
---

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@oakridge.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring Redwood — can you match a CloudArc offer?

Hi Tom — thanks for the details and the PDF.

Quick notes from our side: we don't generally mirror competitor line-by-line, but we can structure an offer that closes the gap on total onboarding economics while preserving predictable unit pricing. To help you present a clear comparison to procurement, I filled out a short fit scorecard for Oakridge (attached). Key points:
- Estimated monthly token usage: 1.6B tokens (peak 2.0B)
- Primary workload: real-time agent completion with strict 95th pctl latency SLOs
- Must-run in US regions; data residency and SOC2 are required

Proposed commercial levers we can consider:
1) One-time migration credit (applied as invoice credit) — sized to net out CloudArc's $150k onboarding credit for first-year migration tasks.
2) Tempo-tiered committed discount (12 months) — structured as a blend of committed units + overage pricing.
3) Dedicated migration concierge (our Solutions Eng team + partner resources) — 4–6 week engagement with defined milestones.

I'm looping Marissa and Karthik to confirm internal approvals and an initial credit cap. Can you confirm whether the CloudArc credit is refundable/contingent on a go-live date, and whether there are usage floors attached? That will impact the shape of an equivalent offer.

Short call today/tomorrow works for me if you want to walk through the scorecard.

— Irene
Irene Choi | Senior Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
attachment: oakridge_fit_scorecard_v1.xlsx

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@oakridge.health>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21 08:37 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring Redwood — can you match a CloudArc offer?

Thanks Irene — quick clarifications:
1) CloudArc's $150k onboarding credit is unconditional; they apply it across the first two invoices.
2) Their 40% discount is on quoted committed run-rate (with a 12-month minimum).
3) The migration engagement is vendor-delivered and they commit a named PM for the 6-week program.

Procurement wants a written counter-offer by EOD 2026-08-24 to include in the vendor review. If Redwood can provide a comparable economics + named migration support, Oakridge will move Redwood to the top of the shortlist.

I can make room for a 30 min slot tomorrow afternoon if you want to present.

— Tom

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-24 09:05 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Oakridge — counter-offer request (need approval)

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Oakridge's clarification. Procurement needs a written counter by EOD today. Below are the options I propose (high level):

Option A — Match-ish (aggressive, requires manager sign-off)
- One-time onboarding credit: $140k applied across first 3 invoices
- 35% off committed run-rate for 12 months (commit: $1.8M ARR equivalent)
- 6-week migration concierge: Redwood SE + partner resources (deliverables: migration plan, infra tuning, go-live playbook)
- SLA: 99.9% uptime + 4-hour incident response for P1 for Dedicated

Option B — Balanced (lower credit, better long-term unit economics)
- One-time onboarding credit: $90k
- 28% off committed run-rate for 12 months (commit: $1.5M ARR equivalent)
- 4-week migration assistance (named SE, limited partner hours)
- Standard SLA

Option C — Pilot-led (minimal risk)
- 8–12 week pilot at a reduced rate (no long-term commit)
- $40k pilot credit for migration support
- If pilot converts within 90 days, convert to a 12-month commitment at 25% discount plus $60k onboarding credit

Notes: legal will need to sign-off on any SLA adjustments and on the credit mechanics (invoice credit vs prepaid). I suggest we include a one-time success milestone (go-live within 10 weeks) to release the full credit.

If you approve Option A, I will submit the written counter and offer a 30-min presentation to their procurement panel today at 3pm PT. If not, I will lead with Option B.

— Irene

Subject: Re: Fwd: Oakridge — counter-offer request (need approval)

Irene — good work on options. Approved to move forward with Option B as the default written counter. Rationale: preserves ARR economics while offering a meaningful onboarding credit and named SE time.

Action items for the counter-offer email (Irene):
- Offer Option B as the primary and mention Option A is available but requires Sales Director sign-off and a 30% credit cap (we don't auto-approve A).
- Provide a concrete migration timeline and named lead (Karthik to be listed as technical lead).
- Include an invoice-credit schedule and milestone release (apply 50% after migrate staging, remainder after production go-live within 12 weeks).
- Include HubSpot deal link and request DocuSign next steps if they accept.

Karthik — please draft the 6-week migration scope for the Option B engagement (bullet list + named deliverables) and share by EOD so Irene can include it in the counter. Legal, please queue SLA language for 28% discount commit.

I'll join the 3pm panel if needed.

— Marissa Cole
Head of Sales — Americas, Redwood Inference
